data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim that separation is necessary is undermined by its own countercondition: if a single engine can verify via symbolic execution that bypasses probabilistic priors, then a same-engine author+checker pair can discover errors without a second training distribution Q. SRC_001 never resolves how 'necessity' survives this admitted self-correction path, leaving the necessity claim overbroad against the problem's requirement to argue whether separation is truly required.
